explanation:
## How Much Does Midjourney Cost? (2026 Pricing Table)

Midjourney charges by **subscription tier**, not per image. The core resource you're buying is **fast GPU time**, measured in hours, which determines how quickly your jobs get processed. Here are all the plans compared:

| Plan | Monthly | Annual (per month) | Fast GPU Hours | Relax Mode | Stealth Mode | Parallel jobs |
|------|---------|-----------------|----------------|------------|--------------|-----------------|
| Basic | $10 | $8 | ~3.3 h (≈200 img) | ❌ No | ❌ No | 3 |
| Standard | $30 | $24 | 15 h | ✅ Unlimited | ❌ No | 3 |
| Pro | $60 | $48 | 30 h | ✅ Unlimited | ✅ Yes | 12 |
| Mega | $120 | $96 | 60 h | ✅ Unlimited | ✅ Yes | 12 |

> The annual discount is the equivalent of **paying for 10 months and getting 12**. It only makes sense if you know you'll be using Midjourney continuously.

---

## How cost per image works

A standard job generates **4 simultaneous variants** at default quality (`--q 1`) and consumes roughly **0.7 minutes of fast GPU time**. From that you can estimate:

- **Basic (3.3 h = 198 min):** ~200 fast jobs → ~800 individual images
- **Standard (15 h = 900 min):** ~900 fast jobs → ~3,600 images (+ unlimited in Relax)
- **Pro (30 h):** ~1,800 fast jobs → ~7,200 images (+ unlimited in Relax)
- **Mega (60 h):** ~3,600 fast jobs → ~14,400 images (+ unlimited in Relax)

**What changes your real consumption:**
- `--q 2` (quality 2) doubles the GPU time per job
- `--turbo` burns **double** the fast hours but generates in seconds
- Upscales, variations and re-rolls also add to the meter
- Forcing `--fast` on Standard and above deducts hours even when Relax is available

---

## Fast Mode vs. Relax Mode

**Fast mode** sends your job to the priority queue — typical wait under 1 minute — and draws down your GPU balance. **Relax mode** (Standard and up) uses a shared queue with wait times of 1 to 10 minutes, but **consumes no fast hours**. That makes total image volume effectively unlimited for users who can afford to wait.

**Turbo mode** (available on Pro and Mega) is the opposite: it generates up to 4× faster than Fast, but consumes **double the GPU hours**. Useful for urgent production iterations.

---

## Extra GPU hours

On any plan you can buy additional fast GPU time at **$4/hour**. Unused hours within the month **do not roll over** to the next cycle — they are lost. That matters when deciding whether to move up a plan or buy loose hours to cover a work spike.

---

## Stealth Mode: what it really means

Without Stealth Mode, **all of your images are publicly visible** in the Midjourney gallery (midjourney.com/explore) and potentially in the community feed. This applies even to prompts generated in private Discord channels or via the API. If you work with confidential client content, unreleased brand concepts or sensitive material, the Pro plan ($60/mo) is the **functional minimum**, not a luxury.

---

## What NO plan includes

- **Brand ownership or exclusivity:** other people can generate similar images with similar prompts
- **Guaranteed long-term storage:** Midjourney can change its retention policies
- **Bulletproof legal rights:** commercial-use terms apply per plan, but the intellectual property of AI-generated images remains a legal gray area in many jurisdictions (check with your legal advisor if it's for intensive commercial use)
- **Unlimited access to older models:** some legacy models may not be available on every plan

---

## Common mistakes when choosing a plan

**"Basic is enough for me"** — True if you generate sporadically. But without Relax Mode, once you exhaust the ~3.3 fast hours the plan grinds to a halt until the next cycle. For regular use, Standard is the most cost-efficient entry point.

**"Pro and Mega are the same except for hours"** — Not exactly. Mega also doubles the parallel jobs versus Standard, which matters if you run production workflows with multiple simultaneous prompts.

**"Hours accumulate"** — They don't. The balance resets every month. If you bought extra hours and didn't use them, they're gone.

**"The annual plan is always the better deal"** — Only if you're certain of constant use. Midjourney has no confirmed prorated refund for early cancellations; review the current terms before committing to a year.

---

## Market context

Compared with the alternatives: DALL-E 3 (via ChatGPT Plus, $20/mo) includes image generation but with monthly credit limits and no Relax Mode equivalent. Adobe Firefly charges per credit (~$5.99/mo for 100 credits). Running Stable Diffusion locally is free but requires your own hardware (a GPU with at least 8 GB of VRAM recommended). Midjourney remains the aesthetic-quality benchmark for many professional creative workflows, which justifies the premium over cheaper options.

faq.q: How much does Midjourney cost per month in 2026?
faq.a: Midjourney has four monthly plans: Basic $10, Standard $30, Pro $60, and Mega $120. Annual billing applies a 20% discount, bringing the effective monthly cost to $8, $24, $48, and $96 respectively. There is no free tier — you must pick a paid plan to generate images.

faq.q: What does Midjourney Basic actually include for $10/month?
faq.a: Basic gives you approximately 3.3 fast GPU hours per month, roughly 200 images at standard quality. There is no relax mode fallback — once your fast hours are used up, you must buy extra time at $4/hour or wait until the next billing cycle. It is best for light, occasional use (under ~10 prompts a day).

faq.q: What is the difference between fast mode and relax mode?
faq.a: Fast mode queues your generation at the front of Midjourney's GPU pool — typical wait is under a minute — and spends your fast GPU hours. Relax mode (Standard, Pro, and Mega) uses a shared slower queue with 1–10 minute wait times but does not consume any fast GPU hours, so your total image count is effectively unlimited. For casual exploration, relax mode is often enough.

faq.q: Is the Standard plan ($30/month) enough for a freelance designer?
faq.a: For most freelancers, yes. 15 fast GPU hours produces roughly 900 fast images, and unlimited relax mode covers exploratory work without burning hours. The main reasons to step up to Pro ($60) are needing stealth mode to keep work private before delivery, or needing 12 parallel jobs for batch production.

faq.q: Which Midjourney plans include stealth mode?
faq.a: Only Pro ($60/month) and Mega ($120/month). Stealth mode keeps your generated images out of Midjourney's public community gallery — essential for client work, unreleased brand assets, or confidential projects. Basic and Standard generations are always publicly visible.

faq.q: Do all Midjourney plans include commercial rights?
faq.a: Yes — all four paid plans (Basic, Standard, Pro, Mega) include commercial use rights for individual creators and most businesses. However, companies with over $1,000,000 in gross annual revenue are required to be on Pro or Mega to retain commercial license rights.

faq.q: How much is Midjourney per year if I pay annually?
faq.a: Annual billing gives a 20% discount across all plans. Basic becomes $96/year ($8/mo), Standard $288/year ($24/mo), Pro $576/year ($48/mo), and Mega $1,152/year ($96/mo). You pay the full year upfront.

faq.q: Can I buy extra fast GPU hours without upgrading my plan?
faq.a: Yes. Midjourney charges $4 per additional fast GPU hour on any plan. This helps with project spikes — for example, if you're on Standard and exhaust your 15 hours mid-month on a large client batch, you can buy 5 extra hours for $20 rather than upgrading to Pro. Note that unused hours do not carry over to the next month.

faq.q: When should I upgrade from Standard to Pro?
faq.a: Upgrade to Pro ($60/month) when: (1) you consistently burn through 15 fast GPU hours before month end, (2) you need stealth mode to keep client or unreleased work private, (3) you want 12 parallel jobs instead of 3, or (4) your business earns over $1M/year (commercial license requirement). If your only issue is occasional extra volume, buying GPU hours at $4/hour is usually cheaper than upgrading.

faq.q: Is there a free tier or free trial in 2026?
faq.a: No. Midjourney removed its free trial in late 2024 and has not reinstated it. You must subscribe to a paid plan to generate images. The cheapest entry point is Basic at $10/month (or $8/month effective on annual billing).

faq.q: How does Midjourney compare to Stable Diffusion in cost?
faq.a: Stable Diffusion is open-source and free to run locally on your own GPU. Cloud Stable Diffusion via APIs (e.g., Replicate) charges per image — typically $0.002–$0.01 per generation — which can be cheaper for very high volumes but needs more technical setup. Midjourney's advantage is a far more polished interface, consistent high quality, and zero infrastructure to manage.
